text:
Dougie Hamilton is 33, playing 20 and a half minutes a night, and doing the job New Jersey pays him for. He has nine points in 18 games, including the power-play goal that sent Saturday's game on Long Island to overtime, and the Devils have 59% of the five-on-five expected goals (the quality of chances) with him on the ice.

His point total is lighter than his play. With him out there, New Jersey has scored 6.4 fewer goals than its chances deserve, which has cost him assists. That usually swings back, and our projection still has him near 39 points.

He's also been in the middle of things: Easton Cowan fought him after a hit on Auston Matthews in Sunday's shutout of Toronto. Evolving-Hockey had him facing the other team's best players (97th percentile competition) and 41st among 215 defensemen in wins above replacement last season. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking adds the part people miss: he stops 18% of the entries aimed at him, against 11% for a typical defenseman.
